articles.detail: 5 cycles, 4 completed; the 18:00 cycle aborted at the selector in 5s on the Claude weekly usage limit and published nothing; 11/12/12/0/15 stories selected against targets of 11/12/13/15/15, avg 9 published per cycle; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one; nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Al Jazeera appears in 12 of 46 articles (26% against 20%), up from 9 of 53. It is the sole source of only two of them and 13% of the day's 95 citations, so this is the multi-source rise to 48% pulling one outlet into many clusters rather than single-outlet dependence. Science is 4 against 5 a day: 0, 1 and 1 against a floor of 2 in the first three cycles, with the feed holding boilerplate and manuscript pages rather than findings, and one whole cycle was lost.
watching: Iran: Tehran and Oman agreed Hormuz routes while the Guards claimed a strike on a gas tanker in the strait, and talks continued in Turkmenistan.
Saudi Arabia: airlines halted Riyadh flights after the Houthi strikes.
UAE: authorities allege a suicide plot behind the flydubai cockpit attack on the Dubai to Tel Aviv flight; truce odds came off their peak.
Ethiopia and Eritrea are mobilising; the selector wants a full report, and the Bloomberg explainer could not be fetched.
Panama: a magnitude 7.7 earthquake toppled buildings and set off tsunami warnings across Latin America.
United States: sanctions on the International Criminal Court, a removal panel convened for Fed governor Lisa Cook, and Hurricane Isaias nearing the Gulf coast.
Brazil: Bolsonaro's runoff campaign is unsettling climate finance.
Ukraine hit a second Yandex data centre, in Kaluga.
coverageGaps: The 18:00 cycle (target 15 stories) published nothing: the selector exited 1 with "You've hit your weekly limit · resets 9pm (UTC)", from a feed of 22 multi-source and 51 niche stories.
Science was under its floor in three of four completed cycles (0, 1 and 1 against 2), and only New Scientist, Ars Technica and MIT Technology Review supplied science, against six outlets yesterday.
Tech fell to 2 against 3 after dedup at 10:00, with nothing usable from Ars Technica, The Register, The Decoder, 404 Media or Hacker News.
Asia had 3 datelines, down from 6, with none from East or Southeast Asia beyond Seoul and Beijing.
Bloomberg page fetches failed in three cycles (source-angles, 10:00, 14:00 and 22:00), and the selector skipped an ECB digital-euro story and the Ethiopia shipping explainer because of it.
Latin America reached 9% on events (Panama City, São Paulo, Mazatlán), still with no Latin American outlet in any feed.
Two stories rest on state media alone: Iran's Caspian water-level plan and the Guards' tanker-strike claim.
context: The four completed cycles averaged 866s (selector 173s, writer 207s, editor 81s), and RSS returned 77 stories in every cycle, so the 22:00 timeouts of 10-08 did not repeat. For the operator: the 18:00 loss was the account's weekly Claude limit, which reset at 21:00 UTC and the 22:00 cycle ran normally; if usage this week tracks last week's, the same cycle is at risk next Friday. Multi-source at 48% and US datelines at 24% are the best readings since the targets were set, on a day one cycle short, so they are not yet a trend. The MercoPress addition to CURATED_SOURCES remains the first experiment to run once the gate lifts on 2026-11-05, after its Event Registry URI is verified.
